doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

title: Babe Barlow and her strip dance
summary: Shade tells of dancer Babe Barlow, who worked with his band and whose strip act went wrong; he rarely went to shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, what about Babe Barlow? You want to tell me
about Babe Barlow? She's in Buffalo, New York.
Yeah. And you say you, did you play for her one time?
No, she used to work with us. That's when she did the strip e dance.
Oh, everything happened. She come and stripping down and stripping down and see the grass patch.
Oh, my God. So, what did she do? She was rad back, huh?

Oh, she was doing that strippy dance, you know, doing all that hollalula stuff and twisting and going on. when she went back on all forward backwards, stripped down, stripped down, stripped to the last piece. And she didn't know it. She was come to find out all the pieces were all with none of them on there. And they said, do it again, she couldn't find it. There was nothing there to do it with.
Did you ever see this show, Mike and Mike? Never did. Never did. She used to be with them. She was a dancer. What did she sing herself?
I don't know. I never did hear.
You never did hear her sing,
I never did go to shows much and fun of much. I would be busy trying to write up my own song and numbers and things like that.
